subject: Post-call: Regional latency & throughput constraints + next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha@finovate.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-14T17:05:00-04:00
Subject: Post-call: Regional latency & throughput constraints + next steps

Hi Samantha / Daniel —

Thanks for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key requirements you called out:
- Latency: p95 generation latency target of <=200ms for US/EU for your 256-token average responses; APAC can tolerate up to ~300ms initially.
- Streaming: first-token/first-chunk latency target <=100ms for chat UI (progressive tokens acceptable).
- Throughput: baseline steady-state throughput of ~6k tokens/sec with short bursts to 20k tokens/sec during peak batch jobs.
- Concurrency: support ~400 simultaneous user sessions with KV cache reuse per session.
- Data residency: EU user request payloads, prompts, and logs must remain in EU regions (no cross-border replication).

Our suggested approach:
1) Run a 2-week PoC with regional routing pinned: US <-> us-east, EU <-> eu-west, APAC <-> ap-southeast. We’ll provision a Dedicated pool for EU to satisfy residency + auditability.
2) Start with the r-instruct-v1 (default quantized) for latency baseline; if we need additional latency headroom we can recommend higher quantization + smaller context variants.
3) Streaming test plan: measure first-byte latency over TCP with 95th/99th percentiles, and validate progressive rendering in your web client.
4) Performance SLOs & SLAs: propose p95 generation latency SLA of 250ms for US/EU (conservative), with SLO targets at 200ms for engineering acceptance.
5) Security/compliance: we’ll provide SOC2 evidence and network isolation diagrams (attaching SOC2 summary and SLO workbook).

Action items / owners:
- Redwood (Prio): run initial performance PoC config and provide test harness + sample load script (Prio: PrIyom Das). Deliver by 10/21.
- Finovate: provide representative prompt corpus (ideally 2000 examples) and traffic shape (peak/hour, diurnal) by 10/17.
- Redwood Sales: prepare pricing for Dedicated EU pool + multi-region routing add-on (Rafael).
- Agreement on success criteria: p95 <=200ms for US/EU during normal traffic & streaming first-chunk <=100ms for 90% of requests.

Attachments: redwood-slo-workbook.xlsx (performance metrics template), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

Would love a quick confirm on the dates above and the priority for EU residency (dedicated pool vs. private deployment). Happy to jump on another 30-minute follow-up if useful.

Cheers,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Regional latency & throughput constraints + next steps

Thanks — details below, keeping it concise for the PoC doc: 

PoC topology (recommended):
- Provision Dedicated pools: eu-west-1 (EU), us-east-1 (US), ap-southeast-1 (APAC). EU pool is isolated (no cross-region read replicas).
- Route by client-region header at the edge; preserve user-shard mapping so EU requests always hit EU pool.
- Use KV prefix caching per-user session to reduce token re-generation.

Fallback / graceful degradation policies:
- Primary: when Dedicated pool in region is healthy, route normally.
- If EU pool reaches defined capacity threshold (e.g., 90% GPU utilization) we will automatically: 1) scale up (if autoscale capacity available); 2) apply intra-region degraded mode — prefer cached completions and switch to smaller context model variant to keep latency.
- If scaling and degraded-mode still insufficient, we will (only with customer-approved config) failover to an EU-compatible hosted variant in the same jurisdiction or contain minimal metadata to EU logs only. We will never route raw EU request payloads to US region without explicit customer opt-in.

Performance target assumptions for PoC (test harness config):
- Test load: steady 6k tokens/sec, weekends/overnight ramp to 20k tokens/sec for batch jobs.
- Concurrency test: validate 400 sustained active sessions + 700 spike tests for 20–30 minute windows.
- Latency goals to validate: p50/p90/p95 for generation; target p95 <=200ms US/EU, <=300ms APAC; streaming first-chunk target <=100ms 90% of the time for US/EU.
- Measurement: use rtt + server-first-byte timestamps; capture percentiles, tail latency, and token/sec throughput.

Data residency / logging:
- EU pool will be configured with customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) and audit-only network egress rules.
- Logs can be stored in EU-only storage buckets; we will provide syslog/ELK forwarding endpoints inside the EU VPC.

I’ll attach a short test-harness README to the PoC folder and provide sample k6/JMeter scripts. If Finovate has network egress constraints (eg. strict IP whitelisting) please share the list so we can include it in the onboarding firewall rules.

—PrIyom
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
